summary: Aspen-Pitkin County Airport (Sardy Field) is a high-elevation mountain airport serving the famous ski resort town of Aspen, Colorado. Sitting at approximately 7,820 feet above sea level and surrounded by the rugged peaks of the Rocky Mountains, it is renowned among pilots as one of the most challenging commercial airports in North America due to its steep approach through mountain valleys. The single-runway facility handles regional jets and turboprops, with most flights operated by regional carriers.
faqs:
Q: Why is flying into Aspen airport considered difficult?
A: The airport's high elevation of about 7,820 feet, combined with surrounding Rocky Mountain terrain, requires specialized pilot training and aircraft certification. Only certain aircraft and crews are qualified to operate there.

Q: Which airlines fly into Aspen-Pitkin County Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by regional carriers including United Express, American Eagle, and Delta Connection, typically using regional jets or larger turboprop aircraft like the Bombardier Q400.

Q: Is Aspen airport open year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates year-round, though winter operations can be affected by snow and mountain weather. Summer brings increased private and charter traffic alongside scheduled service.

Q: How far is the airport from Aspen's downtown and ski slopes?
A: The airport is conveniently located just a few miles from downtown Aspen, about a 10-minute drive, and within easy reach of all four area ski resorts.
transport_tips: Rental cars are available at the terminal, but note that 4WD or AWD vehicles are strongly recommended during winter months for mountain driving. Shuttle services, taxis, and ride-shares operate from the airport, with many Aspen-area hotels offering complimentary pickup. During peak ski season, booking ground transportation in advance is advisable.
local_tip: If your flight options into ASE are limited or expensive, consider flying into Eagle County Regional Airport (EGE), about 70 miles west—it often has more flight choices and lower fares, and the scenic drive over the Continental Divide via Independence Pass (summer only) or I-70 is part of the Colorado experience.
